ground_truth.unit: thermometer points (0-10) per unit proportion of women MPs
ground_truth.location: Table 1, column 1 (Bivariate model), [out-party j's proportion of women MPs (t - 1)]
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Predictors of Out-Party Thermometer Evaluations"), column 1, the reduced-form model without controls.  Ordinary least squares on directed party dyads: the dependent variable is the mean 0-10 feeling-thermometer rating that party i's partisans (respondents who feel close, or a little closer, to party i) assign to out-party j in the Comparative Study of Electoral Systems (CSES) election survey of year t; the regressor is out-party j's proportion of women MPs, lagged one year before the survey and scaled 0 (all men) to 1 (all women).  Sample: every directed pair of parties with at least four MPs each in the year before the survey, in 20 Western democracies and the CSES election studies of 1996-2017 (each pair enters twice, once in each direction).  Country-year fixed effects (the table row reads "Country and year fixed effects"); standard errors clustered by election.

i4r.notes: Blanket I4R verdict (perfect reproduction, team 10); the only per-row entry is an imputation robustness variant (1.890).

ground_truth.unit: thermometer points (0-10) per unit proportion of women MPs
ground_truth.location: Table 1, column 2 (Full model), [out-party j's proportion of women MPs (t - 1)]
ground_truth.context: Table 1, column 2, the full model and the paper's headline estimate (the change in predicted out-party evaluations from moving from zero to all women MPs).  Same dependent variable, regressor, sample, country-year fixed effects and election-clustered standard errors as column 1, adding three controls: the absolute left-right distance between parties i and j in the current election from the Comparative Manifesto Project left-right scale, standardized; a dummy for i and j being governing coalition partners at the time of the survey; and a dummy for i and j both being in opposition (baseline: one governing and one opposition party).

i4r.notes: Blanket I4R verdict; the only per-row entry is an imputation robustness variant (1.741).

deviations_manifest: The paper restricts to dyads where both parties have at least four MPs in the year before the survey. In the data, filtering on the evaluated (to) party's prior seats (to_prior_seats >= 4) reproduces the reported N of 1,842 exactly, while filtering on both parties gives 1,535. I used the to-party filter. Dyads where to_pfeml is missing are dropped listwise.

Elite right-left distance is the dataset's pre-standardized rile_distance_s (standardized over the full 2,266-row dyadic file; its raw mean of 22.4 and SD of 17.6 match the paper's footnote 3), not re-standardized within the estimation sample.
Coalition and opposition partner dummies are govern_together and opposition_together (status at the time of the survey), not prior_coalition and prior_opposition.
The gender-specific DV is 10 - dislike from gender_disagregated_8-8-21.rds (gender 2 = women, 1 = men), with the same to_prior_seats >= 4 filter.
cell.notes: Three exploratory runs (no RESULT lines) inspected the variables, the codebooks (extracted from the .docx with utils::unzip inside the sandbox) and sample-restriction counts. Final model: fixest feols of party_like on to_pfeml (+ rile_distance_s, govern_together, opposition_together in the full model) with cntryyr fixed effects and SEs clustered by cntryyr, for Table 1 columns 1-4. All four Ns (1842/1842/1836/1833) and the 81 elections match exactly. The coefficients are close to Table 1. The largest gaps are the full-model women-MPs coefficient (1.758 vs 1.73) and the opposition-partners coefficient (0.334 vs 0.37). I made no claim-driven changes and never ran check_attempt.
